note: Marquee characters. Parodies carry 'parody'. Edit freely.

fighters.bio: {first} has never truly lost a fight, unless you count the one he lost to a disqualification for elbows so nasty they were declared illegal. Spinning elbows, oblique kicks, and a reach that starts in one zip code and ends in another. Outside the cage, his schedule is 'chaotic' and his press availability is 'theoretical'.

Former plumber's apprentice from Dublin who discovered that talking costs nothing and sells everything. One perfect left hand, one perfect mouth, and a bottomless appetite for equity stakes. Sells more pay-per-views than the rest of the division combined and will remind you of that in every negotiation, press conference and voicemail.

Wrestled bears as a child (allegedly, on camera). Mauls opponents for fifteen minutes while asking them, politely, to give up. Refuses alcohol sponsors, refuses to celebrate with champagne, and refuses to lose. His father's word is law. His mother's word is law with interest. May retire at the absolute peak because he promised someone.

Kickboxing prodigy, anime enthusiast, and the most flexible trash talker in the sport. Walks out doing choreographed dances, fights like a ghost with a grudge, and treats every press conference like a rap battle he already won.

Former tire-shop worker who beat his demons and then beat everybody else. Says about four words per press conference and lets the left hook handle the rest. His hands have been described by doctors as 'geological'.

Worked in a sand mine, crossed a desert and a sea, slept in a parking garage, and now punches harder than a car accident. Very polite. Very calm. Will publicly and patiently explain, with charts, exactly how much you are underpaying him.

Throws 300 strikes a fight and talks to his opponent during most of them. Points at the floor in the last ten seconds and dares you to swing. Everyone loves him, which is a problem for marketing because nobody wants to watch him get punched.

Louisiana's finest export after crawfish. Runs a hot sauce empire, a charity, and a never-ending series of wars against people who talked too much. Will fight anyone, anywhere, as long as there's a bottle of sauce on the table afterwards.

Seventeen hours of cardio, zero filter. Slaps opponents mid-combination to remind them they're being disrespected. Shows up to press conferences late, leaves early, and somehow always wins the press conference.

Learned to fight in Miami backyards and never left the backyard emotionally. Famous for a five-second flying knee and a post-fight description involving a soda. Delivers trash talk like a mob boss reading a grocery list.
Says the most offensive thing in any room he walks into, then wrestles you for 25 minutes without breathing hard. Fans pay to see him lose. He is fine with that, as long as they pay.

Former NCAA wrestler who went from 'boring' to 'terrifying' in the space of one jab. Grinds you against the fence until you question your career choices. Big on business, bigger on the gospel, biggest on reminding you he's undefeated in the division.

Rainbow hair, rainbow tattoos, rainbow knockouts. Streams everything, wears everything, and treats striking like an art project. Got famous on a reality show and stayed famous by putting people to sleep on the way down.

Has more submission wins than most fighters have fights. Grew up in a favela, survived a childhood illness doctors said he wouldn't, and now strangles people with a smile on his face and Jesus on his shorts.
Trained under the Eagle since childhood and talks about him like a holy text. Quiet, devout, and capable of folding you in half like a lawn chair.

Former rugby player who was 214 pounds and decided to be 145. Fights with a clipboard brain and a family-man heart. Responds to trash talk with a slightly confused smile and then a seven-round beating in five rounds.
Predicts the round, predicts the punch, predicts the facial expression of the person he's about to knock out. Has so far been right so often it's becoming a legal issue for bookmakers.
A heavyweight who moves like a welterweight and talks like the nicest bloke at your local pub. Finishes fights before the crowd has found their seats.
Born in Jamaica, raised in Birmingham, famous for one head kick that sent half the sport into hysterics. Quiet, measured, and deeply unbothered by everyone who calls him boring.
Spent years being told he was boring, then won the belt boringly, then held it boringly. Argues with strangers online for sport and has never lost an argument according to himself.
Fights like a man falling down a staircase on purpose and somehow lands on top every time. Nobody can explain his style, including his coaches.
Jabs you for 25 minutes and talks for 25 hours. Every press conference is a live hostage situation for the PR team. Streams his sparring, his opinions and his opinions about your opinions.
D1 wrestler who refuses to wrestle. Fights exclusively in the pocket, chops legs like firewood, and treats every fight like a car crash he paid tickets for.

Liverpool's loudest export since the Beatles. Balloons fifty pounds between fights and posts every cheeseburger. Fans adore him, critics doubt him, and he is perfectly happy to sell both of them tickets.
Gives speeches after wins, speeches after losses, and speeches to the cashier at the grocery store. Comes out of the corner like a golden retriever on espresso.

marquee.archetype: The Funniest Man in the Building
marquee.arc: The Funniest Man in the Building

fighters.bio: Holds the record for most knockouts and most quotable post-fight interviews. Looks exhausted at all times, then knocks you out with one swing while appearing to fall asleep.
Trains by walking on his hands, juggling medicine balls and doing things with a kettlebell that would make a physiotherapist faint. Talks in riddles. Fights like a slasher movie.

Olympic gold medalist who decided his real talent was cringe. Wears a crown to press conferences, calls himself the greatest of all time, and occasionally backs it up, which is the most annoying part.
Shoots takedowns at a rate that should be studied by NASA. Doesn't get tired, doesn't stop smiling, and once tried to carry a teammate around the cage after a win.
Climbs onto opponents' backs like a determined hiker and refuses to get off. Hosts a podcast where he replies to every single critic personally.
Grew up in the Russian Arctic, where the boxing gyms are colder than his stare. Doesn't trash talk, doesn't smile, doesn't stop throwing to the body.
Got cut, came back, became champion, and cried on national television in the most relatable way possible. All of Mexico's flyweight hopes live in his tiny tank top.
Wins every scramble, every chaotic exchange and every staring contest. Calls himself the Cannibal and then apologizes for it.
Karate-based blitzer, devoted dad, and possibly the most polite man to ever deliver a head kick. Has a laugh that sounds like an apology.
Says he'll smash everybody, then does, then asks for three more fights the same night. Wrestles like a hurricane wearing a weighted vest. Shows up sick more often than a kindergarten teacher.

Muay Thai world champion before most of her opponents were born. Practices shooting, tango and spinning back kicks, all with lethal precision. Dances after wins like a ballroom champion who just hospitalized someone.
Former receptionist who decided she'd rather throw people than answer phones. Relentless pressure, explosive throws, and a spinning backfist that has its own fan account.
Shaved head, quiet voice, and a pre-fight mantra that sounds like a meditation app. Then she head-kicks someone into another tax bracket.
Trash talks like she's already won and fights like she believes it. Pulled off one of the biggest upsets in history and has been talking about it ever since, with full justification.
Two-time Olympic judo gold medalist who throws women around like laundry. Cutting weight is the only opponent who's ever given her trouble.

marquee.archetype: The BJJ World Champ Who Wants to Bang
marquee.arc: The BJJ World Champ Who Wants to Bang

fighters.bio: World champion in jiu-jitsu who prefers to stand and swing anyway. Cheerful, loud, and permanently trying to call out someone bigger than him.
Trains by reading samurai philosophy and fighting in forests. Keeps his hands at his waist and his chin in danger, and wins anyway in the most chaotic way possible.
So technically sound he makes main events feel like tax seminars. Nobody wants to fight him. Nobody wants to watch him. Nobody can beat him.
A heavyweight who moves like a dancer and speaks French softly at press conferences. Opponents can't hit him. Fans can't tell if they're bored or mesmerized.
Shoots double legs like his life depends on them and says genuinely funny things in interviews that get him in mild trouble with nobody in particular.
Three-time NCAA champion who believes he's the best fighter alive after six pro fights. He might be right. He might be very, very wrong. Everyone wants to find out.

YouTube star turned boxer who would very much like to fight in your cage, ideally against someone forty years old with two broken legs. Brings forty million followers, his own energy drink, and a lawyer for every occasion.
Arkansas farm boy who hunts his own food, builds his own house and does a twister submission for fun. Has opinions on the shape of the planet that keep the PR team awake at night.
The most avoided man in the division, according to the most avoided man in the division. Wrestles at a pace that should be illegal.
Perth's smoothest boxer. Talks like a surfer, punches like a jackhammer, and politely apologizes to referees for making them work.
Every fight, every finish. Speaks softly, chokes firmly. The kind of man other contenders schedule dentist appointments to avoid.
Point-karate wizard who keeps his hands at his hips and his ego in orbit. Spent a decade at a rival promotion being the most entertaining thing on their cards, and wants you to pay for that history.
The rival league's two-division champion and franchise face. Loyal to them, which means he's the hardest man in the sport to poach and the most satisfying to sign.
The most feared woman in the history of the sport. Has fought for every promotion that would pay her and destroyed everyone they put in front of her.
Comes from the most decorated family in Dagestan and is somehow the scariest striker in it. Won the Lounge's lightweight 'million' and spent it on a gym for 40 cousins.
Taps people with chokes that don't have names yet. Will fight anyone, in any league, for the right number, and will tell you the number on a livestream.
Says nothing, finishes everybody. Won so many tournaments that the Lounge started paying him to stop entering them.
Has held two belts at the same time, which the Lounge's accountants still talk about with fear. Owns gyms, a ranch, and a terrifying overhand right.
Wrestles you for the full 25 minutes and then asks if there's a sixth round. There isn't. He checks every time.
Unbeaten for years by being exactly as exciting as tax season and twice as hard to escape.
The other Edwards brother. Has heard 'are you Leon?' at every airport on earth and has started saying yes.
Has a rear-naked choke so automatic it's been described as 'a subscription service'. Cancellation is not possible.
Younger brother of a showtime kicker, famous for a spinning backfist that turned a whole fight upside down and a press conference that didn't.
Third-generation Hawaiian fighter with a family tree made entirely of left hooks. Two-time Lounge season champion and one-time eater of an entire luau.
Lost to the same woman twice, then knocked the whole narrative out in the third fight. Holds grudges the way other people hold groceries.
World Muay Thai champion who discovered she could also knee people in a cage. Undefeated, terrifying, and very polite about both.
Peru's favourite Lounge champion. Walks out to a marching band, which the Lounge pays for by not paying anyone else.
Won the season, got the million-dollar check, and has explained the tax on it at every press conference since.
Has more guillotine wins than most guillotines. Won the season twice and asked for his prize in sheep. Was refused. Took the check.
Got cut from one league, won a season in another, and now sends the first league a postcard every Christmas.
Six foot eight, eighty-inch reach, and knocks people out faster than the broadcast can play his walkout song.
Has been in every Lounge season since the first one. The playoffs are basically his cottage.
A lightweight who wins rounds the way glaciers win against mountains: slowly, then completely.
Never lost, never smiles, never lets go of a single leg.
Fights MMA on Thursday, boxes on Saturday, and spends Sunday asking why there's no fight on Sunday.
World kickboxing champion who talks about himself in the third person, the future tense and the superlative. Has a lot of followers and an equally large number of opinions about takedowns.
Fought in the first-ever women's main event in the big league, then went and collected belts everywhere else. Still the toughest person in any room she's in.
Took the queen of the flyweights to a split decision once, which in the Lounge's marketing department now counts as 'basically a win'.
A generational talent who has never truly lost a fight and has never truly won one against himself. The cage is the only place his life makes sense. Everywhere else, he's a weekly emergency meeting.
Good fighter. Great podcast numbers. Terrible judgment. Hosts a four-hour stream called 'No Context' where every week he says something that costs you a sponsor.

Every prospect has to pay the toll. Thirty-three fights, zero highlight reels, and a chin carved out of a boat anchor. Nobody wants to fight him and nobody wants to watch him, which is exactly why you need him.
A legitimately dangerous featherweight trapped in the body of a man who has never said no to a buffet. Misses weight with the reliability of a Swiss watch.
Went viral for a spinning backfist knockout in a regional show that took place in a Waffle Hut parking lot. Zero fundamentals, two million followers, and a manager who is also his roommate.

marquee.archetype: The Dad Who Lives Through His Son
marquee.arc: The Dad Who Lives Through His Son

fighters.bio: A shy, decent kid with real talent and a father who screams at referees, judges, promoters and occasionally clouds. Kevin Sr. is his manager, coach, nutritionist and only source of stress.
Fights like she's late for something and parties like the something is cancelled. Equally likely to win a fight-of-the-night bonus and to start a fight at the after-party.
Ex-CPA who still does half the roster's taxes and has started asking very specific questions about yours.
Has fought for five promotions in five years and left each one with a lawsuit and a highlight reel.
Owns four trucks, three of which are impounded. Bets his purse on himself, then on the co-main, then on the NFL. A delight in the cage and a liability everywhere else.
Nobody is sure where his money comes from, including the tax authorities of three countries. Hits like a falling safe.
A good ol' boy with a heart of gold, a truck with no muffler, and a criminal record that is mostly traffic court. Mostly.
